svg.aria-label: Diagram: the three layers of Google Cloud firewall rule nobody writes — always-allowed traffic, the implied actions, and the default network's four pre-populated rules; why the implied ingress action is deny for a VM network interface but allow for an internal load balancer forwarding rule; the default rules opening SSH and RDP to the whole internet and default-allow-internal covering only the auto mode block; and the traffic no rule can block including the metadata server
svg.title: The rules nobody writes: exemptions, implied actions, and the default network's four
svg.text: Default deny inbound is two-thirds true. For some targets the implied ingress action is allow.
Three layers you never wrote: always-allowed traffic, the implied actions, and four default rules.
Three layers of rule you did not write
ALWAYS ALLOWED — rules do not apply at all. Not a permit; an exemption.
IMPLIED ACTIONS — the last step, reached only if nothing matched anywhere.
DEFAULT NETWORK RULES — four real, editable, deletable ingress rules at priority 65534.
Only the third appears in a rule listing. The first two are behaviour, not resources.
The implied ingress action is not always deny
EGRESS — the implied action is allow. Always. That part of the folklore is right.
INGRESS — it depends on the TARGET RESOURCE:
a network interface of a VM instance → implied ingress action is DENY
a forwarding rule of an internal ALB or internal proxy NLB → it is ALLOW
And VPC rules never deny by exhaustion: no match yields goto_next, not a drop.
The default network’s four rules, and the hole in the first
All four are INGRESS, all at priority 65534 — one step above the 65535 floor, so almost
anything you write outranks them. All four can be deleted or modified.
default-allow-ssh — 0.0.0.0/0, tcp:22. default-allow-rdp — 0.0.0.0/0, tcp:3389.
default-allow-icmp — 0.0.0.0/0, icmp. SSH and RDP are open to the whole internet.
default-allow-internal — source 10.128.0.0/9 only, tcp and udp 0-65535 plus icmp.
That source is the AUTO MODE block from #62. A subnet added outside it is NOT covered.
What no rule can block
The metadata server at 169.254.169.254 and fd20:ce::254. It is essential to the instance,
so the instance reaches it regardless of any firewall rules that you configure.
It serves DHCP, DNS resolution, instance metadata and NTP — so blocking egress does not
cut DNS or time. Also exempt: the instance’s own NIC addresses, its alias ranges, its
loopbacks, overlay addresses, and forwarding-rule addresses it is a backend for.
Ingress targets include managed Envoy proxies for internal ALBs and internal proxy NLBs,
which is why the implied ingress action has to be stated per target rather than per network.
The useful reading: nothing here is a rule you can audit by listing rules. Two of the three
layers are documented behaviour, and the one that is editable ships open to 0.0.0.0/0.
